Title: Verify that CORS policy allows only specified HTTP methods
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and a tool to send HTTP requests (e.g., Postman, cURL). The application is running and accessible via the allowed origin (https://no-q:8080).
Steps:
1. Open the HTTP request tool (e.g., Postman).
2. Configure an OPTIONS request to any API endpoint (e.g., /api/appointments).
3. Set the 'Origin' header to the allowed origin: https://no-q:8080.
4. Set the 'Access-Control-Request-Method' header to 'GET'.
5. Send the request and observe the response.
6. Repeat steps 4-5 for 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE', and 'PATCH' methods.

Test Data: Allowed origin: https://no-q:8080
Endpoint: /api/appointments
Methods to test: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH
Expected Result:
1. For GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and OPTIONS methods, the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods' header with the value 'GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS'. The request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK.
2. For PATCH method, the response does NOT include 'PATCH' in the 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods' header. The request may still succeed, but the method is not explicitly allowed via CORS.

Title: Verify that CORS policy allows credentials (cookies, authorization headers) for the allowed origin
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and a tool to send HTTP requests (e.g., Postman, cURL). The application is running and accessible via the allowed origin (https://no-q:8080). User is authenticated and has a valid session cookie or authorization token.

3. Set the 'Origin' header to the allowed origin: https://no-q:8080.

5. Send the request and observe the response.
6. Remove the credentials and send the request again.

Test Data: Allowed origin: https://no-q:8080
Endpoint: /api/appointments/me
Credentials: Valid session cookie or authorization token
Expected Result:
1. With valid credentials and the allowed origin, the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header with the value 'https://no-q:8080' and the 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials' header with the value 'true'. The request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK.
2. Without credentials, the request fails with HTTP status 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden.

Title: Verify that CORS policy does not allow arbitrary headers
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and a tool to send HTTP requests (e.g., Postman, cURL). The application is running and accessible via the allowed origin (https://no-q:8080).
